senses.gloss:
Nītha (‘leading’), neut., means musical ‘mode’ and then ‘hymn of praise.’ The feminine form Nīthā occurs once in the Rigveda meaning ‘artifice.’
Foot notes Rv. iv. 3, 16; vii. 26, 2; x. 92, 3; aitareya brāhmaṇa, ii. 38. Cf. nīthāvid of singers (jaritṛ) in Rv. iii. 12, 5.
i. 104, 5. Cf. the epithet śata-nītha, i. 100, 12; 179, 3; x. 69, 7; sahasranītha, iii. 60, 7; ix. 85, 4; 96, 18 (used of the poet's art, padavīḥ kavīnām).
Cf. Muir, Sanskrit Texts, 1^2, 241.
